top.title: ‘Duty of care’: Players’ union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
top.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. top.title: No winter shopping? Bayern Bosses reveal their stance after injury setbacks
top.description: No winter shopping? Bayern Bosses reveal their stance after injury setbacks Bayern Munich are not planning to enter the January transfer market despite their recent injury problems, according to club president Herbert Hainer. Speaking at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, Hainer admitted that the current situation was not anticipated but insisted that the club does not believe immediate reinforcements are necessary. Luis Díaz is expected to return soon, while Alphonso Davies could be back to full fitness within two weeks. Serge Gnabry is also gradually returning to training. "Therefore, I don't think we need to react in the winter transfer window," Hainer explained. However, the Bayern president acknowledged that circumstances can change quickly, particularly after the club suffered two further injury setbacks, Harry Kane and Michael OIise are both unavailable for the time being, ahead of the AGM. Hainer made it clear that Bayern would be financially capable of reacting if necessary, but stressed that this was not their preferred approach. The club's leadership also remains cautious about January business, with Hainer pointing out that Bayern have not enjoyed much success with signings made during the winter window or in the final days of transfer periods. For now, the Bundesliga leaders are hoping their injured players can return soon enough to avoid the need for additional reinforcements.

top.title: Williams to stay in charge of Swans for Boro trip
top.description: Ashley Williams played more than 350 games for Swansea across eight years [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ashley Williams will remain at the helm for Swansea City's trip to Middlesbrough on Tuesday after taking a point against West Bromwich Albion in his first game as interim boss. Swansea started life after Vitor Matos by coming from behind twice in a chaotic 2-2 draw with the Baggies at the Swansea.com Stadium. Williams, who was seen having a lengthy discussion with Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe after the game, says he has been told he will remain in charge for the midweek trip to face Championship leaders Boro. "I will go to Middlesbrough with the team," Swansea's interim boss said. "I will be concentrating on the build-up to Middlesbrough and the Middlesbrough game, and that is it at that point. "I don't know what happens [after that]. I'm not too interested, if I'm being deadly honest, because all eyes are on Middlesbrough after this. I can tell you that much, and that's it at this point." Williams is leading a caretaker management team also featuring fellow Swansea old boys Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kristian O'Leary following this week's shock departure of Vitor Matos. The 42-year-old, who has primarily worked as a pundit since retiring as a player, said he "absolutely loved" the experience of leading Swansea from the touchline. "To be back here as well was special, and to be with this set of players at this football club is special," he added. Eli Just scored his first goal for Swanse [Huw Evans Picture Agency] "When you're in it, you're concentrating so much that that's all you're thinking about. But when the dust settles and I digest it, maybe this evening or whenever, it's a really proud moment for me. "Even when we went a goal down, I was enjoying it. I was in it with the players. "I wanted them to be aware of me. I wanted them to see me and hear me. If we're suffering for a minute, I'm with them. If we score, I'm with them and I'm happy. It was really nice to feel connected with the team and the whole stadium." Williams' side endured the worst possible start as Isaac Price gave West Brom a seventh-minute lead, but they quickly replied through Moussa Yeo. Rabby Nzingoula then restored Albion's lead before Baggies forward Isaac Price's Panenka penalty was saved by Lawrence Vigouroux. Eli Just swiftly made it 2-2, with the New Zealander also hitting the bar after Melker Widell had struck the post, though Swansea ended up feeling relieved to claim a point as West Brom pushed hard for a second-half winner. "It was end-to-end and very frantic," Williams said. "But my natural thought is just how proud I am of the players and the fans. "To respond after a week like this, an uncertain week, was impressive. Maybe we saw that uncertainty in our team at the start, in the first few minutes, but they recovered themselves." top.title: 'Fragile' Chelsea need to be tougher, says Alonso
top.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing home defeat against Leeds (Henry NICHOLLS) Xabi Alonso warned his "fragile" Chelsea flops to toughen up after their humiliating 4-1 home defeat against Leeds on Saturday. Alonso's side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke's men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. The Blues are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso. Only three teams in the Premier League have conceded more goals than the 20 allowed by Chelsea, prompting Alonso to question his players' mentality. "We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition," the former Liverpool midfielder said. "Today we were in a fragile moment mentally. Confidence that, when we receive a punch, we will not recover." Making his full debut in Alonso's latest bid to find a stand-in for injured striker Joao Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Chelsea were booed off at half-time and again at the final whistle as furious fans showed their displeasure. Alonso pointed to the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo, forced off injured midway through the first half, as the turning point in the game. "After we lost Moises we lost completely the momentum. Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing," he said. "After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed." Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. "I'm not feeling let down. We do it as a team, as a collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen," Alonso said. "There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better." smg/nf

top.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
top.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. top.title: NASCAR Star Tries Bull Riding, Immediately Regrets It
top.description: Kansas City Outlaws bull rider Cassio Dias rides Ricky Vaughn during the championship round on Sunday, April 7, 2024, at Denny Sanford Premier Center in Sioux Falls. NASCAR driver Noah Gragson thought trying bull riding would be an exciting change of pace. Instead, his trip to Davis Rodeo Ranch in North Carolina left him sore for an entire week. The Front Row Motorsports driver climbed aboard two bulls and quickly discovered that handling a race car and staying on a bucking bull require very different skills. Speaking on This Cowboy Life podcast , Gragson described how the soreness began shortly after the experience. “I was pretty good there for a couple hours, and then I got to Olive Garden. We went to Olive Garden afterward in Salisbury, and my neck started getting kind of sore,” he said. A Week of Sore Muscles Gragson said the discomfort worsened the following day. He struggled to raise his arm and described his shoulder as “killing me for the last week.” The soreness also spread through his abdomen and groin, involving what he called “muscles I’ve never used before.” His introduction to bull riding involved two attempts. The first bull offered little resistance, but the second was considerably tougher. Gragson lasted approximately two seconds before getting thrown off. He also described being dashboarded during the experience. By the time he spoke on the podcast, about a week later, he said he was finally somewhat back to normal. Nov 8, 2026; Homestead, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Noah Gragson (4) during the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Unconventional Recovery Methods Gragson even found an unusual way to get some relief during a visit to the Cosmopolitan Casino. He described receiving a massage while leaning over a blackjack table, paying $2 per minute for treatment focused on his neck and back. He credited the massage with helping his traps and neck finally feel better. Gragson finally recovered enough to move freely again after a week of pain. His experience on the ranch in North Carolina remains a painful memory for the NASCAR star : “That was the craziest experience I’ve ever had.”

top.description: Half a million! Bayern reach historic membership milestone among other records FC Bayern Munich have announced that they now have 500,000 registered members , making them the world's largest sports club by registered membership. Their members come from 152 different countries. The announcement was one of several highlights at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, where the club also revealed record financial results for the 2025/26 financial year. Bayern generated a turnover of €988.2 million , an increase of approximately €10 million compared to the previous year. Operating profit rose to €190.8 million, while the club recorded a consolidated net profit of €22.8 million. CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen described the figures as another record year, emphasising the importance of financial discipline and sustainable investment. He also addressed ticket prices, insisting that football must remain affordable for supporters despite the growing commercial demands of the sport. A regular Bundesliga ticket at Bayern currently costs around €80, a price the club has maintained for several years. Meanwhile, president Herbert Hainer praised the club's growing international appeal and highlighted the importance of its partnership with German family-owned business Viessmann. There was also a special message from head coach Vincent Kompany, who thanked the supporters for their backing and described how his family had quickly come to feel at home in Munich.

top.description: Luca Williams-Barnett scored on his first Premier League start (Ben Stansall) Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi hailed 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett as a "special player" after he scored and assisted on his first Premier League start in a 2-0 win over Ipswich on Saturday. The teenager stole the show as Tottenham's upturn continued with a fourth win in five games to climb to ninth in the Premier League table and within three points of the top four. "Luca Barnett is a special player. I am not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think," said De Zerbi in his post-match press conference. The Italian said he had taken the decision to give Williams-Barnett a full debut 10 days ago after he showed flashes of promise in two cameo substitute appearances against Crystal Palace and Leeds. "Yesterday evening when I gave the first eleven... I said to the other players remember the first game, the debut of you (Williams-Barnett) and help the kid tomorrow because he is one of us and if he plays well, we have more chances to win the game." Williams-Barnett showed a poacher's instinct to meet Pedro Porro's cross at the back post to open the scoring on 15 minutes. The winger then ran from inside his own half before producing a perfect cross for Dominic Solanke to tap in Tottenham's second. De Zerbi did not hold back on comparing the England under-19 international to some of the biggest stars in world football if he can match their workrate. "The first day I spoke with Luca and I asked him two things," added De Zerbi. "To play like he plays on the park with his friends with the same freedom and to play and to work hard without the ball like (Ousmane) Dembele, like Raphinha, like (Lamine) Yamal because football is going in a different way and the first defenders are really the attackers. nigeria.title: ‘Duty of care’: Players’ union slams Bayern for Musiala comments
nigeria.description: Global players’ union FIFPRO has slammed Bayern Munich for putting pressure on midfielder Jamal Musiala to renegotiate his contract with the Bundesliga club as he recovers from injury. In a statement issued Saturday, the footballers’ union said recent public comments made by Bayern’s honorary president Uli Hoeness, current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge were part of a “coordinated campaign” to put pressure on Musiala. The Bayern bosses had questioned whether Musiala, who missed several matches with a neurological condition earlier in the season and has recently returned from a hamstring injury, should continue to receive his contracted salary. FIFPRO hit out at “a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations”. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” the international union for professional football players said. “Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala… Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. “Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.” The 23-year-old Germany international signed a contract extension in February 2025 until 2030 and is among Bayern’s top earners. Musiala missed six months after breaking his ankle at the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025. At the start of the 2026-27 season, Musiala collapsed twice on the pitch in pre-season. He later revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”. Speaking Friday after Musiala came off the bench for his first Bayern appearance in two months, Rummenigge suggested the player would not be able to recapture his previous form. “Based on what we know, it unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” Rummenigge said on Sky Germany. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable.” Bayern on Saturday announced record revenues of 988.2 million euros ($1.083 billion) for the 2025-26 season. nigeria.title: REC confirms 2.8m registered voters in Edo
nigeria.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Obo Effanga yest said that the state currently has 2.8 million registered voters. According to him, the last registration exercise raised the figure adding that the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Giving an update on the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection in Benin City, Effanga said a total of 23,401 cards had been collected across the state since distribution commenced on October 9. He explained that the figure comprised 6,319 old PVCs, 5,128 newly produced cards and 11,954 PVCs relating to transfers. Effanga noted, “The state currently has 2.8 million registered voters after the last registration exercise. However, the final figure would be released after the recent clean up exercise by the national body.” The REC disclosed that PVCs for voters who registered during the first and second phases of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise were currently available for collection at INEC offices across the 18 local government areas of the state. The Resident Commissioner said the commission was currently working towards ensuring a smooth electoral process. Speaking on the mock accreditation exercise scheduled for November 28, the REC said the exercise would be conducted in 384 polling units across the state. He said two polling units were selected from each of the 192 wards also known as registration areas for the mock exercise. “The exercise would provide an opportunity to test the commission’s electoral technology and assess the readiness of its personnel ahead of the elections. “The state office had submitted the list of proposed polling units to the commission’s headquarters for approval,” he added. He said the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System would be deployed during the exercise to demonstrate how voters are accredited, how results are captured and how they are transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal. nigeria.title: Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot
nigeria.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. nigeria.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
nigeria.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. nigeria.title: ‘Our Culture’: Deaf Nigerians Embrace Indigenous Sign Languages
nigeria.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”. But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in the country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960. Today, Nigeria, like many countries on the continent with limited education budgets, has a hard enough time placing children in dedicated schools for the deaf and hard of hearing. And there’s even less attention paid to local sign languages used outside the school system — a serious disservice to the country’s linguistic diversity, Festus Zenda, who has worked on documentation projects with local deaf communities, told AFP. “These indigenous signing systems should be studied, documented and preserved before changes in education, migration, technology and wider use of Nigerian Sign Language cause some of them to decline or disappear,” said Zenda, who has helped document the local sign language used by the Tiv ethnic group, in Benue state. A deaf resident gestures with his fingers while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Sani Lawali (3R), a deaf resident gestures with his hands while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Festus Zenda, Deaf Advocate and Indigenous Sign Language Promoter, with Nigeria’s National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), uses sign language to converse during a video call along a street in Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Displacement by formal signing The working-class Abuja exurb of Zuba is a symphony of motorcycle horns, plantain hawkers’ shouts and the dull hum of construction work. Another group adds their own, milder contributions: claps, muffled shouts of exclamation and the swish of rapid hand gestures as they chat in Hausa signs. Nigerian sign languages, like their spoken counterparts, are sometimes confined to a small number of speakers in a country crowded with some 500 tongues and an unknown number of sign languages. But Hausa sign language has become a lingua franca for deaf people across the north of the country. “I cherish my culture, I cherish my indigenous sign language,” Sanni Lawal, who runs a laundry business in Zuba’s crowded market, told AFP through an interpreter. “I want it to expand everywhere.” Nigeria traces its official sign language to Andrew Foster, an American who introduced formal deaf education across a swathe of African countries at the dawn of independence from colonial powers. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
entertainment.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. sports.description: No winter shopping? Bayern Bosses reveal their stance after injury setbacks Bayern Munich are not planning to enter the January transfer market despite their recent injury problems, according to club president Herbert Hainer. Speaking at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, Hainer admitted that the current situation was not anticipated but insisted that the club does not believe immediate reinforcements are necessary. Luis Díaz is expected to return soon, while Alphonso Davies could be back to full fitness within two weeks. Serge Gnabry is also gradually returning to training. "Therefore, I don't think we need to react in the winter transfer window," Hainer explained. However, the Bayern president acknowledged that circumstances can change quickly, particularly after the club suffered two further injury setbacks, Harry Kane and Michael OIise are both unavailable for the time being, ahead of the AGM. Hainer made it clear that Bayern would be financially capable of reacting if necessary, but stressed that this was not their preferred approach. The club's leadership also remains cautious about January business, with Hainer pointing out that Bayern have not enjoyed much success with signings made during the winter window or in the final days of transfer periods. For now, the Bundesliga leaders are hoping their injured players can return soon enough to avoid the need for additional reinforcements.

sports.title: 'Fragile' Chelsea need to be tougher, says Alonso
sports.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing home defeat against Leeds (Henry NICHOLLS) Xabi Alonso warned his "fragile" Chelsea flops to toughen up after their humiliating 4-1 home defeat against Leeds on Saturday. Alonso's side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke's men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. The Blues are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso. Only three teams in the Premier League have conceded more goals than the 20 allowed by Chelsea, prompting Alonso to question his players' mentality. "We need to be tougher. It's something mandatory in this competition," the former Liverpool midfielder said. "Today we were in a fragile moment mentally. Confidence that, when we receive a punch, we will not recover." Making his full debut in Alonso's latest bid to find a stand-in for injured striker Joao Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Chelsea were booed off at half-time and again at the final whistle as furious fans showed their displeasure. Alonso pointed to the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo, forced off injured midway through the first half, as the turning point in the game. "After we lost Moises we lost completely the momentum. Until then we were doing OK, but from that moment they started believing and we started not believing," he said. "After that, we never got the good feeling and were not able to come from the pressure. It completely changed." Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. "I'm not feeling let down. We do it as a team, as a collective. We need to support each other. We need to find solutions to do better because this will happen," Alonso said. "There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. But the physicality, the duels, it's not the only explanation. The mentality part we can do better." smg/nf

sports.title: Nations Championship schedule, results and finals weekend permutations
sports.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship has reached its last weekend of pool play with the finals weekend fate of the world’s top teams becoming clear. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action – and South Africa have pipped New Zealand to top spot in their pool with a bonus point in defeat to Ireland. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how the tables stand ahead of finals weekend. What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. sports.title: NASCAR Star Tries Bull Riding, Immediately Regrets It
sports.description: Kansas City Outlaws bull rider Cassio Dias rides Ricky Vaughn during the championship round on Sunday, April 7, 2024, at Denny Sanford Premier Center in Sioux Falls. NASCAR driver Noah Gragson thought trying bull riding would be an exciting change of pace. Instead, his trip to Davis Rodeo Ranch in North Carolina left him sore for an entire week. The Front Row Motorsports driver climbed aboard two bulls and quickly discovered that handling a race car and staying on a bucking bull require very different skills. Speaking on This Cowboy Life podcast , Gragson described how the soreness began shortly after the experience. “I was pretty good there for a couple hours, and then I got to Olive Garden. We went to Olive Garden afterward in Salisbury, and my neck started getting kind of sore,” he said. A Week of Sore Muscles Gragson said the discomfort worsened the following day. He struggled to raise his arm and described his shoulder as “killing me for the last week.” The soreness also spread through his abdomen and groin, involving what he called “muscles I’ve never used before.” His introduction to bull riding involved two attempts. The first bull offered little resistance, but the second was considerably tougher. Gragson lasted approximately two seconds before getting thrown off. He also described being dashboarded during the experience. By the time he spoke on the podcast, about a week later, he said he was finally somewhat back to normal. Nov 8, 2026; Homestead, Florida, USA; NASCAR Cup Series driver Noah Gragson (4) during the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Unconventional Recovery Methods Gragson even found an unusual way to get some relief during a visit to the Cosmopolitan Casino. He described receiving a massage while leaning over a blackjack table, paying $2 per minute for treatment focused on his neck and back. He credited the massage with helping his traps and neck finally feel better. Gragson finally recovered enough to move freely again after a week of pain. His experience on the ranch in North Carolina remains a painful memory for the NASCAR star : “That was the craziest experience I’ve ever had.”

sports.title: Half a million! Bayern reach historic membership milestone among other records
sports.description: Half a million! Bayern reach historic membership milestone among other records FC Bayern Munich have announced that they now have 500,000 registered members , making them the world's largest sports club by registered membership. Their members come from 152 different countries. The announcement was one of several highlights at Saturday's Annual General Meeting, where the club also revealed record financial results for the 2025/26 financial year. Bayern generated a turnover of €988.2 million , an increase of approximately €10 million compared to the previous year. Operating profit rose to €190.8 million, while the club recorded a consolidated net profit of €22.8 million. CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen described the figures as another record year, emphasising the importance of financial discipline and sustainable investment. He also addressed ticket prices, insisting that football must remain affordable for supporters despite the growing commercial demands of the sport. A regular Bundesliga ticket at Bayern currently costs around €80, a price the club has maintained for several years. Meanwhile, president Herbert Hainer praised the club's growing international appeal and highlighted the importance of its partnership with German family-owned business Viessmann. There was also a special message from head coach Vincent Kompany, who thanked the supporters for their backing and described how his family had quickly come to feel at home in Munich.

The teenager stole the show as Tottenham's upturn continued with a fourth win in five games to climb to ninth in the Premier League table and within three points of the top four. "Luca Barnett is a special player. I am not surprised because his talent is bigger than you think," said De Zerbi in his post-match press conference. "Yesterday evening when I gave the first eleven... Williams-Barnett showed a poacher's instinct to meet Pedro Porro's cross at the back post to open the scoring on 15 minutes. The winger then ran from inside his own half before producing a perfect cross for Dominic Solanke to tap in Tottenham's second. De Zerbi did not hold back on comparing the England under-19 international to some of the biggest stars in world football if he can match their workrate. sports.title: Big blow for Bangladesh! Star player ruled out of second Test against South Africa
sports.description: Bangladesh have suffered a major setback ahead of the second Test against South Africa, with experienced batter Mushfiqur Rahim ruled out of the series finale due to a groin injury. The second Test is scheduled to begin at Centurion on November 23, with Bangladesh needing a victory to level the two-match series after going 1-0 down in Johannesburg. Mushfiqur sustained the injury during the opening Test at the Wanderers, where he complained of acute pain in his left groin. A subsequent MRI scan confirmed inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis, forcing the team management to rule him out of the upcoming contest. Bangladesh national team physiotherapist Bayjedul Islam Khan confirmed the development, explaining that the veteran batter needs immediate rest and a rehabilitation programme to prevent the injury from worsening. "Mushfiqur complained of acute pain in the left groin region during the first Test match. Following the Test, he underwent an MRI scan and the results confirmed some inflammation and irritation around the bony pelvis," Khan said. "He requires immediate rest and targeted rehabilitation to manage the stress response and prevent further aggravation and is unavailable for the second Test," he added. Mushfiqur's absence comes at a difficult time for Bangladesh, who will be keen to bounce back after suffering a nine-wicket defeat in the series opener. The veteran batter had scored 22 in the first innings and 22 in the second innings of the Johannesburg Test. Meanwhile, South Africa have also been dealt an injury setback, with captain Temba Bavuma ruled out of the second Test due to a calf strain. Bavuma is expected to remain with the squad, while Aiden Markram is likely to take over the captaincy. Tony de Zorzi is tipped to come into the playing XI as his replacement. Bangladesh face uphill task to level series The opening Test at the Wanderers saw Bangladesh produce a spirited fightback after an early batting collapse. From 22/3 and later 121/5, they recovered through centuries from Towhid Hridoy (137) and Litton Das (120), who put together a record 206-run partnership for the sixth wicket to take the visitors to 400. South Africa responded with a formidable 557, powered by maiden Test centuries from Marques Ackerman (157) and Ryan Rickelton (102), while Zubayr Hamza contributed 83 and Kagiso Rabada struck a career-best 72. Bangladesh fought back with the ball, but South Africa secured a sizeable 157-run first-innings advantage. In their second innings, the visitors struggled against Rabada and Simon Harmer, eventually being bowled out for 168. Harmer was the chief destroyer with figures of 6/51, while Rabada claimed three wickets. South Africa were left with a modest target of 12 runs and completed the chase to register a nine-wicket victory, taking a 1-0 lead in the series.

sports.title: UFC Qatar results: Ikram Aliskerov puts on suffocating grappling performance to beat Jared Cannonier
sports.description: Ikram Aliskerov wins his fourth in a row (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC) Ikram Aliskerov couldn’t quite get the submission but he used his grappling to drown Jared Cannonier over three rounds to kick off the UFC Qatar main card on Saturday. While he did show off some solid striking early, Aliskerov eventually turned to his wrestling with repeated takedowns and multiple submission attempts to put Cannonier away. The judges scored the fight 30-27 across the board as Aliskerov got the job done by unanimouos decision. Cannonier was aggressive to start, throwing out a good lead jab and mixing in some kicks to the legs. Aliskerov got his attention midway through the round with a hard shot that had Cannonier rattled briefly. Aliskerov’s combinations were starting to connect and his confidence surged as he sought to do damage on the former title challenger. He also scored a takedown to mix things up as the fight moved into the second round. A fence grab from Aliskerov forced a standup from the referee as the action continued back on the feet. But Aliskerov was quick to return to the takedown as he started looking for an arm triangle choke on the ground, although Cannonier defended effectively. Aliskerov eventually hopped on the back and nearly locked on a rear-naked choke but time ran out on the Russian. With five minutes remaining, Aliskerov took Cannonier down again as he sought to control the action while looking to advance his position. Aliskerov snatched onto a kimura but Cannonier resisted and broke free but he was still stuck on the ground. That ground attack allowed Aliskerov to cruise to victory as he gets his fourth win in a row overall while Cannonier suffers a third straight defeat.

Doue went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doue to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doue looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too. In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."

Richard's love affair with outer space started when he saw the original "Star Wars" on TV aged four, and he spent much of the ’90s watching "Star Trek”, "Babylon 5” and “The X-Files" with his mum. But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend. With the Borg overrunning the newly launched USS Enterprise-E, Picard — who has long-standing beef with the Collective, following his assimilation in classic "The Next Generation" story " The Best of Both Worlds " — orders his crew to fight the cybernetic nasties hand-to-hand if required, defying their pleas to activate the ship's self-destruct system and retreat. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit . He didn't say where Ship would be put on display, but the likeliest locale is Starbase, SpaceX's Starship manufacturing and launch hub. (SpaceX plans to shift most Starship launches to its new Starbase Louisiana site, but construction has yet to begin on that $100 billion complex.) Musk participated virtually in the TomorrowX conversation, which was moderated by two friends of his, the venture capitalists Gavin Baker and Antonio Gracias. (TomorrowX took place in Austin, Texas, but Musk was in China on Wednesday as part of President Trump's delegation for his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.) The world's richest man expounded on Ship 42's historic achievement, explaining that it gets SpaceX much closer to the "holy grail of rocketry" — a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. Before Flight 15, SpaceX had already caught Starship's first-stage booster, known as Super Heavy, on three separate occasions , and it had reflown a booster twice. science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
science.description: null Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio. The duo launched — along with a power and propulsion element called the Mercury Transfer Module (MTM) — aboard an Ariane 5 rocket from French Guiana in October 2018 , beginning a long and looping trip through the inner solar system. Mercury is a difficult planet to reach because it's so close to the sun . Spacecraft approaching the solar system's innermost planet are accelerated to high velocities by the immense gravitational pull of our star and must shed a great deal of kinetic energy to be captured by Mercury's much weaker tug. So the BepiColombo team designed a trajectory that featured one flyby of Earth , two of Venus and six of Mercury over the course of about seven years. That flight time was increased by a year , however, after the mission suffered an issue with its solar panels, which reduced the power available for the MTM's electric thrusters. BepiColombo's arrival at Mercury will take a total of about six months. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Today's orbital insertion is the latest milestone in BepiColombo's Mercury arrival phase, which is expected to take about six months in total. Arrival began on Sept. 3, when the MTM released MPO and Mio. The two orbiters remain connected today; they won't separate until Dec. 9 or thereabouts. Shortly thereafter, Mio will settle into its final orbit, a highly elliptical path that will take it over Mercury's poles. MPO is also destined for a polar orbit, though a much less elliptical one than Mio's; the ESA probe will conduct a series of engine burns before finally getting there on March 10, 2027. BepiColombo won't start doing science work until April 6, 2027. The two probes will gather complementary data from their two different vantage points, shedding a great deal of light on a mysterious world. science.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
science.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. science.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.

science.title: GTA hasn't gone to space (yet), but these sci-fi games can offer you a life of crime among the stars
science.description: GTA 6 has only just come out, and it's already taken the world by storm and positioned itself as one of the greatest games of all time . Great news for gamers, but what about sci-fi fans? To this day, Rockstar Games sadly hasn't embraced sci-fi with any of its open-world games (save for those UFO Easter eggs). It doesn't seem likely they'll journey to the stars anytime soon — you can't really do cutting societal satire about space — but that doesn't mean there aren't GTA-adjacent sci-fi adventures set in outer space. The frustrating thing is that no one has exactly cracked that pitch yet. Non-linear games set in outer space tend to be either too ambitious, like No Man's Sky, or too focused on specific experiences like space combat, like Star Wars: Squadrons. The end result is a roster of great sandboxes that let us journey to different star systems, but no game that dares to explore a criminal fantasy with the level of depth and opportunities seen in the last few Rockstar games. With new hardware powering far more complex open-world games, it's only a matter of time before "GTA in space" is a real thing. For now, there are some space games that let us explore sci-fi worlds, roleplaying as criminals and outlaws amongst the stars. Roleplaying a space outlaw (Image credit: Bethesda Softworks) Massive space RPGs like Starfield and The Outer Worlds 2 offer vast playgrounds you can explore and redefine through your actions. The lawful path is the obvious choice if you'd like to save the galaxy, but a life of crime awaits those who tire of the heroics. Starfield even has a "new game plus" mechanic baked into the player's journey, encouraging experimentation and living different lives, so if you stick with the divisive space RPG, the criminal life is all but unavoidable. And in traditional Bethesda fashion, you're not rushed to the next "main" objective, so if you want to become the most dangerous space criminal in the Settled Systems, you'll be supported by the mechanics and systems. You can always get back to saving the galaxy when you feel like it. (Image credit: Xbox Game Studios) The Outer Worlds 2 is another option if you want to become a star-surfing scoundrel. It might not be as absurdly expansive as Starfield, but Obsidian's whole deal has always been freedom of choice and roleplaying, so you can bet this humorous sequel also lets the protagonist become a bit of an a-hole. The main story already sets you in a collision course with corporate interests, too. Like in Mass Effect and other classic space RPGs, it's your choice to be either a goody-two-shoes or an edgy maniac, and I won't lie: the second option is usually more entertaining. Last but not least, there's a third game that also has enough going on to support a GTA-inspired fantasy in outer space: No Man's Sky . It's grown so much over the years that its original space exploration premise has been buried by content like fully customizable space stations, actual cities and towns

science.title: Trouble at Mars: NASA's Perseverance rover, Odyssey orbiter halt science work due to glitches
science.description: null Two of NASA's Mars explorers are sidelined by glitches at the moment. The Perseverance rover and Mars Odyssey orbiter have stood down from science work due to technical problems, NASA announced on Thursday (Nov. 19). Perseverance has been sidelined by an antenna issue, and the venerable Odyssey is dealing with a balky reaction wheel. NASA hopes both can get back to work at Mars by the end of November. Communication issues for Perseverance Perseverance landed inside Mars' Jezero Crater in February 2021, tasked with assessing the area's potential to support past life and with collecting dozens of samples for future return to Earth. It has done all this and more. The Perseverance team has determined that Jezero hosted a potentially habitable lake billions of years ago. And the car-sized rover has found a wealth of complex organic compounds in Martian rock, some of which might themselves be signs of life (though assessing this hypothesis fully will likely require bringing Perseverance's samples to Earth for analysis, scientists stress). In addition, Perseverance just set a new distance record for off-Earth driving, rolling past the mark set by its smaller cousin, NASA's Opportunity rover (28.06 miles, or 45.16 kilometers). Perseverance broke that record on Oct. 11. Just 19 days later, however, the mission team noticed a problem: The rover's main UHF downlink radio — which it uses to send information home to Earth, via data-relay satellites in Mars orbit — failed to send its usual "heartbeat" pings to the main computer. Perseverance detected this problem autonomously and reacted as it was programmed to do: The six-wheeled robot switched to its backup UHF radio and went into a protective "safe mode," shutting down all non-essential systems. The rover team recovered Perseverance from safe mode but soon noticed another issue: "The backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output," NASA officials wrote in an update on Thursday . Perseverance's handlers have stopped using that backup radio as well; the rover is now communicating with Earth directly (without the help of relay orbiters), sending signals to NASA's Deep Space Network dishes via its high-gain antenna. This pathway features lower data rates, and the mission team wants to prioritize the delivery of diagnostic information. So they've paused Perseverance's science work, which includes observations by its various cameras. The glitch may be disappointing to devoted Perseverance fans, many of whom have already noticed that the mission website hasn't uploaded any new raw images since Nov. 7 . But there's no reason to panic, according to NASA. "The rover is stable and communicating with the team," agency officials wrote in Thursday's update. "The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November, and NASA will provide further updates in the future as the team works the issue."
